nodes.label: `tagMayServe()` admits a legacy bare-tag release on the download path only when the route's own asset predicate matches, while the update routes keep T7's stricter rule
nodes.norm_label: legacy bare tag asset compatibility stage
nodes.rationale: [05 - Conversations/home-belajarcarabelajar-proyek-snipset/2026-09-27 - t8-download-routing-retry [ses_f1d526ca4ffejy210M5YRuZFhy].md:L5266] The reason the stage exists: "a bare-tag release may be admitted on the download path only when it actually carries the file that route serves; a namespaced other-platform release is never borrowed. Isolation must still hold" — which is what lets `/deb` keep serving the pre-namespaced `v0.6.849` Linux files that a Windows-only reading of the tag had rejected.

nodes.label: After a git checkout restored a file, its mtime moved again — proof a second live process was still writing the same allowlisted file

nodes.rationale: [05 - Conversations/home-belajarcarabelajar-proyek-snipset/2026-09-27 - t8-download-routing-retry [ses_f1d526ca4ffejy210M5YRuZFhy].md:L3657] The detection itself is the anchor-worthy fact: `index.js` was 15452 bytes at `2026-09-27 18:46:48.866053629`, two minutes AFTER the checkout, which the note dates itself at [same file:L3670] "The file changed at 18:46:48, after my checkout at ~18:44:50. Something else is writing this file.", with the diffstat grown from 15 insertions / 28 deletions to 197 / 212. The consequence, stated at [same file:L6773]: "My 18:48 write clobbered that session's `index.js`, which is unrecoverable — I rebuilt from the test contract." This is the mirror of `concept--shared-file-clobber-by-checkout`, where nine agents' work was destroyed by the checkout; here the direction is reversed and the destroying agent is the writer.

nodes.label: Reverting a catalog key to its own literal cannot fail a behavioural test; the informative mutation must change the value, not the spelling
nodes.norm_label: value identical rename is mutation immune by construction
nodes.rationale: [05 - Conversations/home-belajarcarabelajar-proyek-snipset/2026-09-28 - convert-string-literals-to-catalog [ses_f17699444ffe9mvKVnkec6mwn9].md:L8328] "Reverting the conversion to the literal did NOT fail a test (2/2 passed) — and it cannot, by construction: `SOUND_EFFECTS.TOGGLE` and `"toggle_001.ogg"` denote the same string, so no behavioural test can tell the two spellings apart. That is the point of the refactor, but it means the instruction as literally written is unsatisfiable." The substitute that does bite is at [same file:L8329]: swapping the key to `SOUND_EFFECTS.CLICK` failed with `expected "vi.fn()" to be called with arguments: [ 'toggle_001.ogg' ]`, which pins the filename and transitively proves the mapping is value-correct.

nodes.label: A JSX attribute cannot take a bare constant identifier, so two rewrite passes colliding at identical offsets produce invalid JSX that only a type check catches
nodes.norm_label: jsx attribute requires a brace expression for a constant
nodes.rationale: [05 - Conversations/home-belajarcarabelajar-proyek-snipset/2026-09-28 - convert-string-literals-to-catalog [ses_f17699444ffe9mvKVnkec6mwn9].md:L4585] "In JSX, `attr=identifier` (without braces) is INVALID syntax — JSX attribute values must be a string literal or a brace expression. `soundEffect=SOUND_EFFECTS.SCRATCH` will fail to parse." The mechanism is stated at [same file:L4589]: the plain-literal pass and the JSX pass matched the same quote at the same offset, and a stable sort let the plain literal win the dedupe. The fix and its verification are at [same file:L8316] — run the JSX pass first and claim its quote ranges, with `tsc --noEmit` as the load-bearing check that found it.
